title: Form Largest Integer With Digits That Add up to Target
summary: Given an array of digit painting costs and a target cost, find the largest possible integer whose digit painting costs sum exactly to the target.
statement: Given an array of digit painting costs and a target cost, find the largest possible integer whose digit painting costs sum exactly to the target. The integer must not contain any zeros and must be returned as a string; if no such integer exists, return '0'.
constraints: cost[d-1] is the cost of appending digit d; use total cost exactly target.
Return the numerically largest positive integer, or "0" if impossible.
hints: DP over each achievable total cost, storing its best digit string.
Extend a prior exact-cost state with every digit whose cost fits.
Compare candidates first by length, then lexicographically, and keep digits descending.
Longer positive integers are always larger; for equal lengths lexicographic order is numeric order.
editorial: Longer positive integers are always larger; for equal lengths lexicographic order is numeric order.

tests.explanation: Four digits are possible, and descending 7772 is the largest.
Two nines cost sixteen, so the optimal exact-cost result is 85.
